display.title: Episode 443: The Strange Beggar, Chapter 1 (Chai Elul)
display.summary_short: Before Chai Elul, Uncle Yossi explains why a birthday matters, and begins the serial 'The Strange Beggar' about a scholar offered a post as town rabbi.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Chai Elul 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that Chai Elul is the birthday of both the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, and teaches what a birthday means: the day Hashem sent your neshamah down from Gan Eden, when your mazal is strong, a time to take stock of the past year and make good resolutions. He reminds children to know their Hebrew birthday and offers Tzivos Hashem's help in finding it. After the Hakochainik march and the pushka, he explains from Rashi that the Shema is a 'secret weapon', and a first-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites it. Story time begins 'The Strange Beggar': Rabbi Yisrael, a poor Torah scholar, is invited to become rabbi of a nearby town. Before accepting, he wants to know whether its people are kind, charitable and united, and he comes up with a plan. The chapter ends there. A listener's letter tells how he shared Torah stories with new friends from day camp, and the show closes with the sponsor and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Use your birthday to take stock and resolve to grow in Torah and mitzvos; share what you know with friends.
